Apprenticeships and Work Experience
Clare Vertigen is a long time member of the Education and Skills subgroup and Managing Director of the South West Apprenticeship Company. She has kindly put together this guide to help you find an apprenticeship.
Step 1: Understanding apprenticeships
Before diving into applications, get to grips with what apprenticeships actually involve.
A great place to start? The Institute for Apprenticeships and Technical Education (IfATE) and their Occupational Maps: Occupational Maps: Institute for Apprenticeships and Technical Education. This site breaks down apprenticeship levels, required skills, progression routes, and even how they’re assessed. It’s always good to know what you’re applying for!
Step 2: Finding an apprenticeship vacancy
Now for the harder part – actually finding the vacancies. Apprenticeships are competitive, so casting a wide net is key! Register on the Government’s ‘Find an Apprenticeship’ site (and set up alerts). Sign up to job boards like Indeed and UCAS and, again, set alerts.
Research big employers – Not all companies list their vacancies on job boards. Many have dedicated Early Careers or Apprenticeship pages on their websites, or they recruit via open days.
Look at local training providers and Further Education colleges. They often have connections with businesses and can help match applicants with opportunities.
Step 3: Standing out from the crowd
Here’s where most applicants slip up – they think qualifications alone will land them the role. Nope!
Employers aren’t just looking for good grades; they want:
A genuine passion to learn
An interest in their company and industry
A great attitude and ability to fit into their team
Companies invest time and money into their apprentices, so they want someone who really wants the opportunity.
Tip: Research the company – not just what they do, but their values and mission. Show them why you want to be part of their team!
Apprenticeships are competitive, but with the right approach, you, your son or daughter or grandchild can secure an amazing opportunity.

Work Experience & Work-Related Learning at SGS Forest High
At SGS Forest High we are committed to preparing our students for the world beyond the classroom. Currently, our students in Key Stage 4 (Years 10–11) have the opportunity to take part in a one-week work experience placement which they arrange themselves. This gives them a real taste of life in the workplace, helping them develop skills, confidence, and a better understanding of different careers.
Looking to the future, we are planning to build on new government guidance by expanding our work-related learning programme to include Key Stage 3 (Years 7–9). This means that all our students will benefit from career-focused activities from an earlier age, giving them even more opportunities to explore different career paths and develop essential skills.
Government Requirements:
The UK government recommends that schools provide meaningful work-related learning opportunities, ensuring that all students can gain experience and insight into the world of work:
Our careers programme is guided by the Gatsby Benchmarks, a set of standards for high-quality career guidance in schools. These benchmarks help ensure that students have access to meaningful experiences and informed career advice.
Our Approach at SGS Forest High
By providing these opportunities, we aim to equip our students with the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to make informed choices about their future careers. We are proud to work closely with local businesses and community partners to make these experiences possible.
Employers
Get Involved with Our Careers Programme
We are always looking to strengthen the links between our students and the local business community. Your involvement can make a real difference in helping young people explore career paths, develop skills, and make informed choices about their futures. There are a variety of ways you can get involved:
We are proud to currently work with a range of local and national organisations, including:
We also love to involve our alumni, who can offer unique insights into career paths, share their own experiences after leaving school, and act as role models for current students. Hearing from former students helps our young people understand the real-world possibilities that lie ahead.

Careers Education at SGS Forest High School
Career education plays a crucial role for SGS Forest High School in Cinderford, located in the Forest of Dean, due to its unique socio-economic challenges and historical context.
Historically an ex-mining town, Cinderford has faced significant economic shifts following the decline of the mining industry. This transition has left a lasting impact on the community, including a lack of employment opportunities and economic diversification. Career education can serve as a vital tool in revitalising the local economy by equipping students with the skills and knowledge needed to pursue new career paths in various industries.
One of the primary challenges in Cinderford is the lack of transport infrastructure, which can severely limit students’ access to job opportunities and educational resources. Many residents may find it difficult to commute to larger cities or towns for work or further education, thus making local career education programs even more essential. By providing career training and education at SGS Forest High, students can develop the necessary skills to secure employment without the need to travel long distances. This not only improves individual livelihoods but also helps retain talent within the community, fostering local economic growth.
Moreover, career education can address the skills gap that often exists in post-industrial towns. As the economy evolves, there is a growing demand for workers skilled in technology, construction, healthcare, and renewable energy sectors. By introducing a diverse range of opportunities that cover a range of industries that focus on these areas, SGS Forest High can better prepare its students for the jobs of the future. This proactive approach could attract new businesses to the area, drawn by a skilled and ready workforce, thereby further stimulating the local economy.
In addition to economic benefits to the local community, career education can also have significant social impacts. It can empower individuals with a sense of purpose and direction, reducing unemployment and associated social issues such as poverty and crime. For our students, access to career education can inspire them to pursue higher education and professional careers, breaking the cycle of limited opportunities that may have affected previous generations.
Furthermore, community engagement and partnerships with local businesses and educational institutions can enhance the effectiveness of career education programs. Collaboration with employers can ensure that training programs are aligned with the actual needs of the job market, increasing the employability of graduates. Involving local stakeholders also helps build a supportive network that encourages continuous learning and development within the community.
Our Vision and Commitment
At SGS Forest High School, we aim to be a school where every child learns and every child grows because every child matters. Our careers education programme is built on this foundation.
We are committed to:
For Students, Parents, Teachers and Employers
This careers section is designed for everyone in our school community. Whether you’re a student exploring your future, a parent or carer guiding your child’s journey, a teacher enriching learning with real-world context, or an employer looking to inspire and support the next generation, this is your starting point.
Explore the sections below to find:
Together, we’re not just preparing students for the world of work, we’re helping shape the future of our community.

At SGS Forest, all Year 10 students will receive one-to-one careers guidance from an independent fully qualified Level 6 Careers Advisor.
After their session, students will be given personalised notes summarising the discussion. These, along with recommended resources, useful websites, and tailored advice, will be uploaded to Unifrog, where students can access them at any time for future reference.
As a Registered Careers Development Practitioner, Mrs Booker can also offer careers advice and guidance to support students with their future pathways.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At Forest High School, we believe that every child deserves the opportunity to thrive, achieve their potential, and feel valued as part of our school community. We are committed to providing a supportive, inclusive, and nurturing environment where students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) can flourish both academically and personally.
Our dedicated SEND team works closely with students, families, staff, and external agencies to ensure that appropriate support is in place to meet individual needs. We recognise that every learner is unique, and we strive to provide personalised support that enables all students to access the curriculum, develop independence, build confidence, and experience success.
We value strong partnerships with parents and carers and encourage open communication throughout each student’s journey with us. Together, we aim to create positive outcomes and ensure that every young person feels supported, included, and empowered to reach their full potential.
On this page, you will find information about our SEND provision, the support available, key contacts, and useful resources for students and families.

Enrichment Activities
We are excited to launch our new Enrichment Activities Programme from September 2026, giving Key Stage 3 students the opportunity to explore new interests, develop skills, and broaden their learning experiences beyond the classroom. Our enrichment activities will take place every Friday during period 5.
Our first ‘Friday Funday’ programme will offer a range of engaging activities including Choir, Chess Club, Media Mindfulness, Cadets, Crafted by Nature, Dance, Public Speaking, Paper Possibilities and 0-5k Jogging.
Mrs Rivers will be supporting the implementation of these exciting opportunities, helping to provide our students with a greater breadth of learning, creativity, wellbeing, and personal development at Forest High School.
Looking ahead, we hope to expand the programme over time to include activities such as baking, swimming, and many more opportunities that make the most of the beautiful natural environment in which we live. We also aim to roll out the programme across all year groups in the future, ensuring that even more students can benefit from these exciting experiences. We look forward to seeing our students discover new passions, build confidence, and create lasting memories through Friday Funday.
Supporting our Programme
To help us deliver and grow these exciting opportunities, we are seeking support from local businesses and organisations. Funding and donations will enable us to invest in equipment, resources, specialist activities, and new experiences for our students. If you are a business that would be interested in supporting our Friday Funday Enrichment Programme through sponsorship, a donation, or the provision of resources, we would love to hear from you. Your support can make a real difference in helping our students access a wider range of enriching opportunities. Please get in touch with us at info@foresthigh.org.uk to discuss how you can support this exciting initiative. Together, we can help our young people thrive and reach their full potential.

Safeguarding and Support
Support and Early Help
Whisper (Report a Concern)
Here at SGS Forest High School we:
Have a culture of fairness and equality;
Care for each other;
Listen to our students;
Teach our students to keep safe;
Support students and their families and carers;
Identify signs of concern;
Monitor attendance rigorously;
Communicate regularly with external agencies;
Train all our staff/Governors in safeguarding;
What is Safeguarding & Child Protection?
Here at SGS Forest, we are committed to the safeguarding and protection of all our young people, it involves:
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our young people and this requires all staff, Governors, visitors, parents/carers and students to share this commitment.
We aim to ensure that all child protection and welfare concerns and referrals are handled promptly, sensitively, professionally and in ways that support the specific needs of the individual child. Through providing a caring, safe and stimulating environment which promotes the social, physical and moral development of all our students, we aim to foster an atmosphere of trust, respect and security, which allows our students to flourish and go onto lead positive and fulfilling lives beyond school.
The SGS Academy Trust Safeguarding Young People and Vulnerable Children Policy and procedures can be viewed and downloaded here.

Online Safety
Guide for Parents and Carers
At SGS Forest High School, keeping students safe online is a key part of our commitment to their wellbeing. We understand that the digital world offers amazing opportunities, but it also comes with risks. That’s why we take a proactive approach to online safety, providing both technical safeguards and education to help students navigate the internet responsibly.
Our Approach to Online Safety
In school, we have robust systems in place to protect students from inappropriate or harmful online content. These are monitored carefully by staff and regularly reviewed to ensure their effectiveness. Any online safety concerns are recorded and handled according to our policies. We teach students how to stay safe online, use digital tools responsibly, and behave respectfully in digital spaces. By embedding these lessons into everyday learning, we aim to give students the knowledge and skills they need to make positive choices online.
Personal Development Curriculum
Online safety is an important part of our Personal Development curriculum, which is delivered throughout all year groups. Lessons cover a wide range of topics, including:
By integrating online safety into Personal Development lessons, students are able to explore scenarios, discuss risks, and develop practical strategies to protect themselves and others in real-life situations.
Safe and responsible use of social media
Recognising and responding to cyberbullying
Online Risks and Social Media
Many social media platforms (such as Instagram, Snapchat, and Facebook) have a minimum age of 13, and WhatsApp has recently raised its age limit to 16. These limits exist to protect young people from:
It is important for parents and carers to be aware of these risks and to help children navigate the online world safely.
Exposure to inappropriate or harmful content
Contact from strangers or potential online predators
Pressures to share personal information or images
How Parents and Carers Can Help
It is the responsibility of parents and carers to set clear boundaries at home and monitor their child’s online activity. Working together with school, parents can help reinforce safe and responsible online behaviour.

Responsible Internet Use
The law makes it illegal for anyone to send offensive, threatening, or false material online with the intention of causing distress. Children can be held legally responsible for their actions online from the age of 10. Teaching responsible internet use is therefore essential.

Year 11 Information Hub
This page has been created to support our Year 11 students and their families throughout this important academic year. As students begin their final year at Forest High School, there will be plenty of key information, deadlines, opportunities, and events to keep track of, and this hub aims to bring everything together in one convenient place.
Throughout the year, you will find important dates, exam information, revision resources, intervention opportunities, post-16 guidance, letters home, and updates designed to help students achieve their very best.
Year 11 is an exciting and rewarding year, but we know it can also feel challenging at times. We are committed to supporting every student on their journey and helping them feel confident, prepared, and ready for the next stage of their education.
We look forward to celebrating the successes, achievements, and memorable moments of the Class of 2027 throughout the year.
Together, let’s make it a fantastic final year at Forest High School.
